_source: Bagholder Association long video (owner's favourite reference), 591K views on a 10.8K-subscriber channel, 2 months old. Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19: frames every 2-3 s for 0-77 s while the audio probe ran, then seeks at 150/229/318/323.5-325 (0.7 s highlight burst)/476/565/712/868/926/1060 s; word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (2,318 words over 1,046 s of speech, about 131 words a minute overall, about 135-150 inside a chapter). Our own descriptions; shots after 77 s are spot samples, not a full list. Times of the first 77 s from the probe's picture-change list. Narrator kind is a guess (we can't hear it): an even pace with no breaths in the captions reads as a synthetic voice.

lines.gist: Sets out how huge the brand is worldwide, with counts and sales.
It rules fast food in China and owns a holiday in Japan.
But in its home country the empire is shrinking.
Gives its fall to fifth place and its smaller home spending.
Names the three rivals that passed it.
Paradox: people eat more fried chicken than ever, yet it lost.
Asks how the category's inventor lost its own market in a boom.
The founder's era: the bucket as the family dinner, cheap and unbeatable.
Habits moved to boneless food eaten in cars; its slow fryers could not keep up.
First rival wins with one product, fast drive-throughs; per-store sales five times higher.
Second rival strips the menu to tenders and wins young buyers.
Third rival's viral sandwich moment while the brand's big ad budget did nothing.
Why it couldn't fight back: old buildings and franchisees who won't pay to remodel.
Abroad it built modern stores from scratch and localised the menu.
At home stores shrank and spending fell, leaving it fifth.
Three lessons: inventing a category, scale without flexibility, nostalgia.
Asks viewers which chain they pick and whether a comeback is possible.

whyItWorks: Opens on evidence, not a face: a real annual-report table with the figure already highlighted, so frame 0 is a fact.
Every figure is backed by a document on screen: article screenshots with a yellow highlighter wiping across the exact sentence.
A paradox stated by 45 s (demand at a record, the brand losing) sets one open question the whole film answers.
Chapters are silent 4-5 s title cards with a music drop, 5 of them, each named like a mechanism (the trap, the assault).
